subject.title: fix: harden aerith native hook relay recovery

question: Should lost-relay PreToolUse ever no-op when loop detection was expected but core OpenClaw approval policies could still apply?
rationale: The current PR trades native-tool availability during Gateway recovery against fail-closed approval behavior, and that security boundary needs explicit maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Preserve approval boundary first
options.body: Require the unavailable-mode decision to account for all core approval policies, or keep PreToolUse fail-closed whenever the tool payload could require approval.

options.title: Accept loop-only no-op explicitly
options.body: Land a documented carveout only if maintainers intentionally accept the approval tradeoff and the PR includes live recovery proof for that exact path.

options.title: Defer to canonical restart fix
options.body: Pause or close this PR if the preferred owner-boundary fix is the narrower stale-relay restart and regeneration work already represented by related relay fixes.

recommendation.title: Preserve approval boundary first
recommendation.body: Require the unavailable-mode decision to account for all core approval policies, or keep PreToolUse fail-closed whenever the tool payload could require approval.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent ownership signal across native relay recovery, approval policy, docs policy, and full-suite tooling surfaces.
